final_candidates.decision_summary: Position 473 is verified as Asp and corresponds to the conserved OCT1 TM11 aspartate that electrostatically coordinates cationic substrates; Asn is isosteric and charge-neutral, so binding/translocation should be abolished with minimal impact on folding or membrane abundance.

Complete removal of the essential carboxylate at the verified D473 site should eliminate cation coordination; the small cavity created lies in a solvent-accessible translocation pathway and is unlikely to destabilize the transporter.

Cys substitution at the same critical aspartate is a classic SCAM-style replacement that typically preserves folding and surface expression while ablating function; ranked third because thiol chemistry leaves a small chance of partial residual coordination.

stop_reason.detail: Additional LLM-only rounds cannot add new information beyond the already mechanistically converged D473 (canonical D474) binding-site set.

history.rationale: This Asp (canonical OCT1 D474, offset by one because the sequence given starts at Pro2) is the key cation-coordinating carboxylate in the TM11 central binding site; Asn is isosteric so charge is neutralized with minimal folding/expression penalty.

Position 473 in this (Met-less) numbering equals canonical hOCT1 D474, the conserved TM11 aspartate that coordinates the cationic substrate; Asn is isosteric and charge-neutral, so it should abolish cation binding with minimal folding/abundance penalty.

Complete removal of the essential negative charge in the substrate cavity should abolish organic-cation binding/translocation; Ala is well tolerated sterically in a buried helix and unlikely to block trafficking.
Removes the essential carboxylate entirely; small cavity created is likely tolerated in a solvent-accessible translocation pathway, so transport loss with retained expression is probable.
Cys substitution at this critical Asp is a classical loss-of-transport mutation in OCT1 cysteine-scanning work while the transporter remains membrane-inserted.

Cys substitution at this aspartate is a classic SCAM-type replacement that is well folded but non-functional; slightly lower confidence than Asn/Ala due to possible partial residual coordination/reactivity.
Glu385 (canonical E386) lines the central cation-binding cleft and contributes an anionic contact; Gln neutralizes charge conservatively, likely killing transport without destabilizing the fold.
E385 here corresponds to canonical E386, the second acidic pocket residue proposed to bind organic cations; Gln is isosteric and neutralizing, giving loss of function at low folding risk.
Alanine deletes both charge and side-chain bulk at this binding-site glutamate, giving a stronger functional knockout, with modestly higher risk of altered helix packing than E385Q.
Kept as a backup to E385Q but demoted because Ala is less isosteric and largely redundant with the Gln variant at the same site.

Trp216 (canonical W217) is a core aromatic of the OCT1 substrate cage providing cation-pi contacts; truncation to Ala should eliminate substrate recognition, though the cavity-facing location keeps folding risk moderate.
W216 (canonical W217) is a core cation-π pocket residue; Trp→Ala should abolish substrate binding, though the large cavity carries some destabilization/abundance risk.

Arg438 (canonical R439) forms the conserved salt-bridge/charge pair with the binding-site Asp and is needed for the alternating-access cycle; charge removal should block translocation while the protein still traffics.

R438 (canonical R439) likely forms an intramolecular ion pair supporting the acidic binding site and the conformational cycle; neutralization should block transport but its network role adds folding uncertainty.
Tyr360 (canonical Y361) contributes an aromatic/hydroxyl contact in the substrate pocket; Ala removes both interactions and is expected to strongly impair transport with limited stability cost.
Y360 (canonical Y361) lines the cavity, but loss of a large aromatic in a TM bundle may reduce stability/abundance, so it is ranked below isosteric pocket edits.
Phe158 (canonical F159) is a pocket-lining aromatic that packs against the substrate; loss of this bulky side chain should disrupt binding, though it is more buried and carries some misfolding risk.
F158 sits in a packed TM region; Phe→Ala there is a stronger candidate for misfolding/reduced abundance than for a clean transport-null phenotype.
